name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
description: Adversaries abuse command and script interpreters such as PowerShell, cmd and bash to execute commands and scripts.

name: PowerShell
description: Adversaries abuse PowerShell to run commands and scripts, often with encoded commands (-enc), hidden windows, download cradles (DownloadString, IEX) and in-memory execution.

name: Obfuscated Files or Information
description: Adversaries obfuscate payloads or commands, e.g. string concatenation or Base64 encoding, to evade detection.

name: Ingress Tool Transfer
description: Adversaries transfer tools or files from an external system into a compromised environment, e.g. via download cradles.

name: Valid Accounts
description: Adversaries use credentials of existing accounts to gain access, persistence or privilege escalation.

name: Brute Force
description: Adversaries systematically guess passwords when credentials are unknown. Typical indicators are many failed logins from one source in a short window.

name: Password Guessing
description: Adversaries guess passwords against accounts, for example repeated SSH or RDP login attempts against a single host.

name: Password Spraying
description: Adversaries try a small number of common passwords across many accounts to avoid lockouts.

name: Remote Services: SSH
description: Adversaries use SSH with valid or guessed credentials to log into remote systems.

name: Remote Services: Remote Desktop Protocol
description: Adversaries use RDP with valid or guessed credentials to control remote systems.

name: Network Service Discovery
description: Adversaries scan remote hosts for open ports and services. Indicators: many short flows with SYN packets and resets to many destination ports from one source.

name: Active Scanning
description: Adversaries probe victim infrastructure with network traffic to gather information before an attack.

name: Scanning IP Blocks
description: Adversaries scan IP ranges and ports to identify live hosts and exposed services.

name: Network Denial of Service
description: Adversaries flood a network service with traffic (e.g. SYN floods) to degrade or block availability. Indicators: extreme packet rates with few responses.

name: Endpoint Denial of Service
description: Adversaries exhaust resources of an endpoint or service to deny availability to legitimate users.

name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
description: Adversaries steal data by sending it over an existing command and control channel.

name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol
description: Adversaries exfiltrate data using protocols other than the primary C2 channel, e.g. FTP, DNS or HTTPS to external hosts.

name: Exfiltration Over Web Service
description: Adversaries use legitimate external web services to exfiltrate data. Indicator: very large outbound transfers to external addresses.

name: Application Layer Protocol
description: Adversaries communicate over application layer protocols such as HTTP(S) to blend in with normal traffic.

name: Non-Standard Port
description: Adversaries communicate over ports not typically associated with the protocol, e.g. 4444, 1337 or 8888.

name: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism
description: Adversaries bypass mechanisms that control privilege elevation, such as UAC or sudo.

name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
description: Adversaries exploit software vulnerabilities to elevate privileges.

name: Account Manipulation
description: Adversaries manipulate accounts, e.g. adding users to the local Administrators group, to maintain or elevate access.

name: Create Account: Local Account
description: Adversaries create local accounts to maintain access, e.g. net user /add.

name: Permission Groups Discovery
description: Adversaries enumerate groups and permissions, e.g. net localgroup administrators.

name: System Owner/User Discovery
description: Adversaries identify the primary user or privileges of a system, e.g. whoami /priv.

name: OS Credential Dumping
description: Adversaries dump credentials from the operating system, e.g. with Mimikatz.

name: OS Credential Dumping: LSASS Memory
description: Adversaries access LSASS process memory to obtain credential material (sekurlsa::logonpasswords).

name: Inhibit System Recovery
description: Adversaries delete backups and shadow copies (vssadmin delete shadows) to prevent recovery, commonly before ransomware.

name: Data Encrypted for Impact
description: Adversaries encrypt data to interrupt availability, e.g. ransomware renaming files with a .locked extension.

name: User Execution
description: Adversaries rely on users opening malicious files, e.g. an Office document spawning PowerShell.

name: Phishing
description: Adversaries send phishing messages to gain access to victim systems.

name: Data Staged
description: Adversaries stage collected data in a central location before exfiltration.

name: Archive Collected Data
description: Adversaries compress or encrypt collected data (e.g. 7z archives) prior to exfiltration.

name: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
description: Adversaries add programs to Run keys or the Startup folder for persistence.

name: Scheduled Task
description: Adversaries abuse the Windows Task Scheduler to execute malicious code.

name: Masquerading
description: Adversaries manipulate names or locations of artifacts to appear legitimate, e.g. renamed tools in public folders.
